notes: Everything here came out of one Assetto Corsa session. Every turn arrow in AC pointed the wrong way: GOAT read the corner's direction from the curvature of your reference map and treated that as the same calculation for every sim, but iRacing's map is a latitude/longitude projection while Assetto Corsa hands out two axes of a left-handed world, so every AC lap was drawn as its own mirror image. Eight of the nine corners at the Renault test track were backwards. GOAT now calibrates the map against your own steering, whose direction convention per sim is known and tested. iRacing is unchanged. The Stint window was showing YESTERDAY's stint, stuck on turn 1: the state file carries a timestamp that nothing ever read, and that old stint pre-dated corners carrying a position, so the list could not scroll. Stints older than six hours are ignored now, and when GOAT genuinely cannot tell where you are it shows the list from the top instead of guessing at turn 1. Its type is readable too - the 'lap 24, 22% on target' line and the turn numbers were fixed at ten point in the grey used for disabled controls; both scale with the window now and sit in the normal text colour. The TV angles option is finally part of its button rather than a tab stuck to the side, and the overlay's SETS menu no longer runs off its own panel when seven or eight overlays are open.
